chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Jamil, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

There will be three miles between the two congregations, meaning Friday prayer will not be held except in what is between them and three miles. Friday prayer is not valid except with a sermon. And if there are three miles between the two congregations in the Friday prayer, there is no harm if these [people] combine [the prayers] and these [people] combine [the prayers].

key_terms.يُجَمِّعَ: To combine (prayers, specifically Dhuhr and Asr)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on combining Friday prayers when the congregation is spread over a distance of three miles?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a practical flexibility in Friday prayer logistics, permitting separate congregations to perform combined Dhuhr and Asr prayers if the distance between them is three miles and a sermon is delivered. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on removing hardship for the community while maintaining the essential elements of the Friday prayer, such as the khutbah. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the conditions under which the obligation of gathering in a single location can be relaxed due to spatial dispersion.
